payload.executive_summary: Candidate B02A selects architecture option O2 (task-parallel fan-out/fan-in) to minimize wall-clock time by executing independent implementation lanes in parallel while preserving CouncilOS governance: deterministic orchestration, strict stage handoffs at every transition, JSON-only canonical artifacts, RFC 6901 evidence pointers, RFC 6902 repair-only for JSON, diff-only patchsets for code, and a dedicated deterministic integration merge/validate/review/patch sub-flow before Judge→Freeze. The plan emphasizes integration-risk mitigation (notably merge conflicts K12 and regressions) via namespaced workspace partitions, lane-scoped gates, and a single integration checkpoint where all parallel outputs are merged and revalidated under orchestrator-controlled deterministic ordering and budgets.

architecture_choice.rationale: O2 best matches branch B02's priority on speed for divisible work by enabling parallel Generate→Validate→Review→Patch lanes while retaining deterministic governance. The main trade-off—higher fan-in integration risk (merge conflicts, cross-lane regressions, reproducibility hazards)—is explicitly managed with a governed Integration sub-flow (deterministic merge ordering, conflict reporting/escalation, full-repo validators, integration-focused review) and a two-level acceptance strategy: lane-level scoped gates first, then integrated system-level gates prior to Judge→Freeze.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: Intake validates plan_package_final.json + repo_context.json + workspace_context.json and initializes immutable run_manifest + append-only event_log. Work planner compiles work_plan.json with a dependency DAG and deterministic lane partitioning hints. Parallel lanes each run Generate (produce diff-only patchset artifacts) → PatchApply (orchestrator-applied) → Validate (lane-scoped validators, secrets scan) → Review (findings-only) → Patch (bounded repairs with smallest-passing selection), emitting stage_handoffs at each transition and writing to namespaced workspace partitions. Completed lane patchsets then fan-in to Integration: deterministic merge/apply in a fixed order → full-repo Validate → integration Review (findings-only) → integration Patch as needed. Judge consumes integrated outputs plus lane/integration findings and produces evidence-backed decisions + trace_report; Freeze assembles the Implementation Freeze Bundle only if all closure gates pass.
key_design_decisions: Parallelize only lane-executable work; reserve all cross-lane coupling resolution to a single deterministic Integration stage to reduce nondeterminism at fan-in.
Use namespaced workspace partitions per lane plus a canonical integration partition to contain side effects and simplify traceability and context-pack bounding.
Define deterministic merge/apply ordering rules that are independent of wall-clock completion timing to preserve reproducibility.
Enforce two-level gating: lane-scoped validators must pass before integration, and integrated full-repo validators must pass before Judge→Freeze.
Keep reviewers strictly findings-only across both lane and integration reviews; all writing/patching remains with writer/patcher roles under orchestrator control.
Treat integration conflicts and cross-lane regressions as first-class artifacts (conflict/integration reports) that drive deterministic escalation (patch → reroute → HITL → ChangeRequest).

milestones.name: Intake + Contract Schemas + Baseline Governance Gates

deliverables.text: Typed/versioned schemas (or schema specs) for repo_context.json and workspace_context.json, including required fields for path protections, tool entrypoints, partition rules, retention/compaction, and access-control declarations.

Intake validators and structured rejection behavior for missing/schema-invalid canonical inputs; initialization of immutable implementation_run_manifest.json and append-only implementation_event_log.jsonl.
Evidence-pointer compliance validator (RFC 6901 objects only) and secrets scanning/redaction/blocking guardrails integrated into pre-persist validation paths.
Tool permission matrix policy-as-data for all stages used by O2 (including IntegrateAndValidate), with deny-by-default and explicit repo-write-via-patch_apply-only enforcement.

exit_criteria: AT2 and AT3 pass (repo_context/workspace_context required and schema-validated before relevant stages).
AT8 passes for run_manifest immutability and event_log append-only behavior.
AT10 and AT11 pass (single evidence pointer standard; no non-JSON evidence).
AT19 and AT20 pass (tool policy enforcement logged; secrets blocked prior to persistence).

milestones.name: Work Planning DAG + Deterministic Lane Partitioning + Stage Handoff Backbone

deliverables.text: work_plan.json compiler/spec including dependency DAG, parallelism annotations, deterministic lane IDs, and task-to-AT# trace mapping hooks.

Stage state model for O2: Intake → Parallel Lanes (Generate/Validate/Review/Patch) → Integration (Merge/Validate/Review/Patch) → Judge → Freeze, with explicit checkpoint boundaries and required stage_handoff artifacts at every transition (including per-lane and integration transitions).
Workspace partitioning rules: per-lane partitions plus a canonical integration partition; unified workspace_index.json accounting across partitions with provenance metadata.

exit_criteria: AT4 passes (recorded stage sequence includes at minimum Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze, with checkpoint boundaries at every transition; additional O2 stages are allowed but must still be checkpointed).
AT5 and AT6 pass (a stage_handoff exists for every stage transition and contains required resumable fields and evidence pointers where applicable).
No plan-semantics deviation pathways exist without ChangeRequest+decision+escalation (R16) in the work planning outputs.

milestones.name: Parallel Lane Execution Loops (Generate→PatchApply→Validate→Review→Patch) with Lane-Scoped Gates

deliverables.text: Per-lane orchestrator behavior: spawning lanes with deterministic budgets, per-lane stage_handoffs, and lane completion signaling with artifact_refs for patchsets and validation outputs.
Diff-only patchset artifact contract and deterministic apply order; enforcement of forbidden/protected paths and operation/size caps during PatchApply.
Lane-scoped validators emitting structured test_results.json and quality_reports.json (with deterministic AT# mapping where applicable) plus secrets scans at each checkpoint.

Role separation enforcement in lanes: reviewers are findings-only; patchers produce RFC 6902 JSON Patch for JSON artifacts and replacement diff-only patchsets for code repairs; orchestrator applies smallest-passing-repair selection deterministically.

exit_criteria: AT9 passes (reject prose/markdown/unstructured canonical outputs; accept schema-valid JSON-only artifacts).
AT12–AT15 pass (JSON Patch-only for canonical JSON repairs; diff-only patchsets; forbidden/protected path enforcement + op caps; deterministic smallest-passing selection).
AT22 passes (writer/reviewer/judge separation and multi-vendor routing recorded; reviewers emit findings-only).
AT23 passes (deterministic retry budgets recorded; escalation path exercised when budgets exceeded).

milestones.name: Deterministic Integration Fan-In (Merge→Validate→Review→Patch) and Conflict/Regression Governance

deliverables.text: Integration merge/apply engine with deterministic ordering independent of wall-clock completion timing; requires explicit base_commit in each lane patchset; emits merged repo_snapshot.json and an integration ordering record.

Structured conflict/integration reporting for K12-class issues (overlapping diffs, apply failures, inconsistent base/head metadata), including deterministic escalation triggers and required stage_handoffs.

Integration validator suite executing full-repo gates (build/test/lint/typecheck/security/secrets as applicable via repo_context entrypoints) and producing integrated test_results.json + quality_reports.json.
Integration review findings-only pod focused on cross-lane interactions and system-level quality; integration patcher loop for bounded remediation prior to Judge.

exit_criteria: Integration stage always blocks Judge entry unless all lane-scoped gates and integrated gates meet policy (two-level acceptance).

Deterministic integration ordering and conflict escalation behavior is documented and testable under K12 scenarios (conflicts beyond thresholds trigger deterministic reroute/HITL as defined by policy).
Secrets, tool-policy, and evidence-pointer validations continue to pass at integration checkpoints (no weakening of M1 controls).

milestones.name: Judge + Freeze (System-Level Trace, Closure Gates, Freeze Bundle Assembly)

deliverables.text: Judge evaluation artifact expectations: evidence-backed trace_report.json across lane + integration artifacts, and a decision output that enforces evidence-pointer completeness for all approvals/waivers.

Freeze assembler outputs the minimum Implementation Freeze Bundle set (CNS10/R7) from integrated state plus required lane artifacts as specified by the bundle contract, with final integrity/reproducibility/workspace-integrity checks.

Final closure-gate enforcement: Freeze denied unless build/test/lint/typecheck/security/secrets/integrity/workspace integrity/risk closure/reproducibility/trace completeness gates all pass under deterministic retry policy.

exit_criteria: AT7 passes (Freeze Bundle contains all minimum required artifacts and directories).
AT21 passes (Freeze denied when any closure gate fails; permitted only when all pass).
AT8 passes at end-to-end scale (audit spine immutability/append-only properties preserved through the full O2 run).

decision_log.question: Which architecture option will this candidate implement?
decision_log.choice: Select O2 (task-parallel fan-out/fan-in with a governed deterministic integration sub-flow).
decision_log.rationale: Branch B02 prioritizes wall-clock speed for divisible work; O2 directly supports parallel lanes with a deterministic fan-in stage to manage merge conflicts/regressions while preserving stage gating, audit spine, and role separation requirements.
what_would_change_this_decision: If the expected work is tightly coupled with frequent cross-file conflicts (high K12 likelihood), O1 may be preferred for lower integration complexity.
If long-horizon execution with frequent budget exhaustion is the norm, O3 may be preferred for partial-freeze/resume-first semantics.
If system boundary simplicity outweighs modular governance (and internal controls can be proven), O4 could be reconsidered.

decision_log.question: How will acceptance be enforced under parallelism?
decision_log.choice: Two-level acceptance: lane-scoped gates must pass before fan-in, then integrated system-level gates must pass before Judge→Freeze.
decision_log.rationale: This matches the branch acceptance strategy and mitigates late surprises by ensuring each lane meets scoped quality/integrity requirements while still requiring full-repo validation after merge to catch cross-lane regressions.
alternatives_considered: Only integrated validation (simpler, but higher rework risk and slower debugging)
Only lane validation (faster, but unsafe for cross-lane interactions)
what_would_change_this_decision: If repositories are fully modular with proven non-interference and very costly full-repo validators, consider reducing integrated validation scope (still keeping a minimal integrated gate set).
If validators cannot be meaningfully scoped per lane, shift emphasis to integrated gates and treat lane gates as lightweight prechecks.

decision_log.question: How will deterministic reproducibility be preserved when lanes complete at different wall-clock times?
decision_log.choice: Integration merge/apply ordering is deterministic and independent of completion timing (e.g., order by lane_id and patchset sequence), and each patchset must declare base_commit metadata for applicability checks.
decision_log.rationale: Parallel execution introduces nondeterminism in completion order; making merge/apply order a pure function of declared identifiers preserves replayability and avoids race-dependent integrated states.
alternatives_considered: Attempt automatic conflict resolution with heuristic ordering
what_would_change_this_decision: If upstream requirements mandate chronological ordering for audit semantics (unlikely), incorporate timestamps only as non-authoritative metadata while keeping ordering deterministic via a stable sort key.
If integration policy requires dependency-based ordering, base the order on the work_plan DAG topological sort (still deterministic).

decision_log.question: What is the workspace strategy for parallel lanes?
decision_log.choice: Namespaced per-lane workspace partitions plus a canonical integration partition; unified workspace_index.json accounts for all items with provenance and versioning.
decision_log.rationale: Partitioning reduces accidental cross-lane contamination, enables smaller lane-scoped context packs, and supports clean fan-in with explicit provenance. A unified index is still required for auditability and context-pack determinism.
alternatives_considered: Fully isolated workspaces with no unified index
what_would_change_this_decision: If the workspace backend cannot support namespacing/access control reliably, fallback to a single workspace with strict path-based partition rules enforced by validators and tool sandboxing.

decision_log.question: How will merge conflicts and integration regressions (K12) be handled under O2?
decision_log.choice: Treat conflicts/regressions as first-class integration artifacts (conflict/integration reports) that drive deterministic escalation: attempt bounded integration patching within op caps; if thresholds exceeded, reroute/HITL per policy; never silently resolve conflicts without recorded evidence and deterministic rules.
decision_log.rationale: K12 is the dominant risk introduced by parallelism. A governed integration stage with explicit artifacts and thresholds avoids silent, non-reproducible conflict handling and preserves auditability and escalation discipline.
alternatives_considered: Allow automatic conflict resolution by tools without structured reporting
Push conflict resolution back into lanes (can cause oscillation and duplicated effort)
what_would_change_this_decision: If repos have extremely low conflict rates and high confidence in deterministic auto-merge, thresholds can be tuned upward—but still require reporting artifacts and audit logging.
If conflicts are frequent and expensive, reconsider O2 in favor of O1 or adjust lane partitioning rules to reduce overlap.

decision_log.question: What governance posture will be used for tool access and HITL strictness?
decision_log.choice: Sandboxed tooling with deny-by-default permissions and medium HITL strictness, focusing HITL interrupts on integration-level findings, protected-path touches, security/secrets events, retry-budget exhaustion, and any ChangeRequest/waiver.
decision_log.rationale: This aligns with branch posture: accept integration complexity for speed while containing risk via deterministic enforcement and targeted HITL at high-leverage choke points (notably integration fan-in and policy exceptions).
alternatives_considered: High HITL strictness at all lane transitions (safer but slower)
Low HITL strictness with mostly automated handling (faster but riskier for K12/K4/K7)
what_would_change_this_decision: If operating in a high-compliance environment (regulated repos, production deployment coupling), raise HITL strictness and expand mandatory approvals.
If historical data shows very low defect rates and strong validator coverage, consider reducing HITL interrupts while keeping mandatory triggers for secrets/security/protected paths.

decision_log.question: How will role separation be enforced across parallel lanes and integration?
decision_log.choice: Enforce writer/reviewer/judge separation per stage and across all lanes via orchestrator routing and output-type allowlists; reviewers emit findings-only artifacts and cannot produce patchsets or JSON patches; judges emit decisions/waivers only.
decision_log.rationale: Parallelism increases opportunities for accidental self-review; enforcing separation as an orchestrator-validated invariant preserves governance (CNS12/R22) while still allowing concurrency.
alternatives_considered: Allow lane-local combined writer+reviewer for speed
Allow integration reviewer to author patches for faster resolution
what_would_change_this_decision: Only if an explicitly governed policy change permits combined roles (would require ChangeRequest and approval), which is outside baseline constraints.

decision_log.question: How will deterministic 'smallest passing repair' selection work in a parallel setting?
decision_log.choice: Apply R15 selection within each lane repair cycle and within integration repair cycles separately, using deterministic tie-breakers (fewest operations → fewest bytes → first-generated), with candidates recorded and comparable under the same validator suite.
decision_log.rationale: Parallelism can produce multiple passing candidates simultaneously; applying the same deterministic selection rule at each repair scope (lane/integration) prevents subjective choice and preserves reproducibility.
alternatives_considered: Global selection across all lanes at once
what_would_change_this_decision: If repairs interact across lanes (shared files), defer selection to integration scope only (still deterministic) or reduce lane independence assumptions via revised partitioning rules.

synthesis_warnings.summary: O2 relies on deterministically specified lane partitioning rules, deterministic merge/apply ordering, and explicit conflict-resolution thresholds; these must be concretely defined and validated to avoid K12-class nondeterminism and to meet reproducibility expectations.

Several blocking open questions remain for enforceable implementation (e.g., repo ecosystems/validator commands, workspace backend constraints, diff format/normalization, deterministic smallest-repair scoring and conflict-resolution policy details). These uncertainties can prevent a fully testable, implementation-ready O2 plan without upstream clarification.
